notes.title: Equating nouns with 是
notes.explanation: Use 是 (shì) to link two nouns, like 'am', 'is', or 'are' in English. Don't put 是 before simple adjectives.

examples.english: I am a student.
He is a teacher.

notes.title: Yes/no questions with 吗
notes.explanation: Add 吗 (ma) to the end of any statement to turn it into a yes-or-no question without changing word order.

examples.english: Are you Chinese?
Do you drink tea?

notes.title: Negating with 不
notes.explanation: Place 不 (bù) directly before a verb or adjective to negate present, habitual, or future actions and states.

examples.english: I am not a teacher.
Today isn't cold.

notes.title: Bounce-back questions with 呢
notes.explanation: Attach 呢 (ne) after a noun or pronoun to ask 'What about ...?' or 'Where is ...?' based on context.

examples.english: I'm fine, how about you?
Where is my book?

notes.title: Negating 有 and past actions
notes.explanation: Always use 没有 (méiyǒu) instead of 不 to negate 有 ('don't have') or to say something did not happen.

examples.english: I don't have a cat.
He didn't go to school yesterday.

notes.title: Asking 'what' with 什么
notes.explanation: Keep 什么 (shénme) in the exact spot where the answer goes, rather than moving it to the front of the sentence.

examples.english: What is your name?
What would you like to eat?

notes.title: Pointing with 这 and 那
notes.pattern: 这 / 那 + Measure Word + Noun
notes.explanation: When 这 ('this') or 那 ('that') comes before a noun, place a measure word such as 个 or 本 between them.

examples.english: This book is very interesting.

examples.pinyin: Nà ge rén shì wǒ bàba.
examples.english: That person is my dad.

notes.title: Possession and modifiers with 的
notes.explanation: Use 的 (de) after a pronoun or noun to show ownership, much like ''s' in English. It can be dropped for close family.

examples.english: This is my computer.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì Wáng lǎoshī de xuésheng.
examples.english: He is Teacher Wang's student.

notes.title: Linking adjectives with 很
notes.explanation: Put 很 (hěn) before an adjective to form a natural statement; it often acts as a neutral link rather than strong 'very'.

examples.english: It is hot today.
Chinese is interesting.

notes.title: Expressing 'too' or 'so' with 太…了
notes.explanation: Wrap an adjective between 太 (tài) and 了 (le) to express 'too ...' or enthusiastic 'so ...!'.

examples.english: This dish is so delicious!
Today is too cold.

notes.title: Counting nouns with measure words
notes.explanation: Mandarin nouns require a measure word after a number. 个 (gè) is the general default when no specific classifier applies.

examples.english: I have two friends.

examples.pinyin: Zhuōzi shàng yǒu yí ge píngguǒ.
examples.english: There is an apple on the table.

notes.title: Asking small numbers with 几
notes.explanation: Use 几 (jǐ) to ask 'how many' when expecting a small number (roughly under 10), always paired with a measure word.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ jiā yǒu jǐ kǒu rén?
examples.english: How many people are in your family?
What time is it now?

notes.title: Telling the time with 点
notes.explanation: Put the hour before 点 (diǎn, o'clock) and minutes before 分 (fēn). Use 半 (bàn) for half past the hour.

examples.english: It is nine in the morning now.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bā diǎn bàn qù gōngzuò.
examples.english: I go to work at eight thirty.

notes.title: Completed action or new state with 了
notes.pattern: Verb + 了 + Object  /  Clause + 了
notes.explanation: Placed after a verb, 了 (le) marks a completed action; at the end of a sentence, it signals a change or new situation.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ mǎi le yì bēi chá.
examples.english: I bought a cup of tea.
It started raining.

notes.title: Asking 'where' with 哪儿
notes.pattern: Subject + 在 + 哪儿? / 去 + 哪儿?
notes.explanation: Place 哪儿 (nǎr) right where the location answer belongs, after 在 ('to be at') or a movement verb like 去 ('to go').

examples.english: Where do you study?
Where did Mom go?

notes.title: Locations before actions with 在
notes.explanation: When saying where an action happens, put 在 (zài) + place BEFORE the main verb, never at the end of the sentence.

examples.english: I eat at home.
He works at the hospital.

notes.title: Learned skills and future with 会
notes.explanation: Use 会 (huì) before a verb for a skill you learned (like speaking a language) or to say something will happen.

examples.english: I can speak a little Chinese.
Will it rain tomorrow?

notes.title: Wishes and plans with 想
notes.explanation: Put 想 (xiǎng) before a verb to politely express 'would like to' or 'want to'.

examples.english: I would like to drink some water.
Tomorrow I want to go to the store.

notes.title: 'All' or 'both' with 都
notes.explanation: 都 (dōu, 'all / both') always goes BEFORE the verb or adjective, never after it as in English.

examples.english: We are all students.
I like all of these books.

notes.title: Asking 'how' with 怎么
notes.explanation: Place 怎么 (zěnme, 'how') directly in front of the verb to ask how an action is done or how to get somewhere.

examples.english: How do you write this character?
How do we get to the train station?

notes.title: Wanting and 'going to' with 要
notes.explanation: Use 要 (yào) for direct wants ('want'), ordering items, or actions you are about to do.

examples.english: I want a cup of coffee.
I am going to the airport this afternoon.

notes.title: Permission and possibility with 可以
notes.explanation: Put 可以 (kěyǐ) before a verb to ask for or grant permission ('may / can'). Use 不能 (bù néng) to refuse.

examples.english: May I sit here?
You can take a short rest today.

notes.title: Adding 'also' with 也
notes.explanation: Just like 都, the adverb 也 (yě, 'also / too') must stand after the subject and before the verb or adjective.

examples.english: My older sister also likes dancing.

examples.pinyin: Tā hěn lèi, wǒ yě hěn lèi.
examples.english: He is tired, and I am tired too.

notes.title: Superlatives with 最
notes.explanation: Place 最 (zuì) before an adjective or feeling verb (like 喜欢) to express 'the most' or '-est'.

examples.english: I like playing basketball the most.
This road is the closest.

notes.title: Giving directions with 往
notes.explanation: Use 往 (wǎng, 'towards') followed by a direction word before a motion verb like 走 ('walk') or 开 ('drive').

examples.english: Walk straight ahead.
Please look to the left.

notes.title: Distance between places with 离
notes.pattern: Place A + 离 + Place B + 很近 / 很远
notes.explanation: Use 离 (lí) to measure how close or far Place A is from Place B, always placing the adjective at the end.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā lí gōngsī hěn jìn.
examples.english: My home is very close to the company.
Is the airport far from downtown?

notes.title: Attitude or effect with 对
notes.explanation: Place 对 (duì) + target before the verb or adjective to show who or what an action or feeling is directed toward.

examples.pinyin: Duō hē shuǐ duì shēntǐ hǎo.
examples.english: Drinking plenty of water is good for your health.
The teacher is very kind to the students.

notes.title: Ongoing actions with 正在
notes.explanation: Put 正在 (zhèngzài) before a verb to show an action is happening right now, like English '-ing'.

examples.english: My younger sister is doing her homework right now.
It is snowing outside right now.

notes.title: 'Already' with 已经…了
notes.pattern: Subject + 已经 + Verb / Adj + 了
notes.explanation: Put 已经 (yǐjīng, 'already') before the verb or adjective, and pair it with 了 at the end of the clause.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǐjīng chī guò zǎofàn le.
examples.english: I have already eaten breakfast.
It is already getting late.

notes.title: Continuous states with 着
notes.explanation: Attach 着 (zhe) right after a verb to describe an ongoing posture or state, such as wearing clothes or keeping a door open.

examples.english: The door is open.

examples.pinyin: Tā chuān zhe yí jiàn hóng yīfu.
examples.english: She is wearing a red outfit.

notes.title: Past experiences with 过
notes.explanation: Follow a verb with 过 (guò) to talk about whether you have ever done or experienced something before.

examples.english: I have been to Beijing.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ kàn guò zhège diànyǐng ma?
examples.english: Have you ever seen this movie?

notes.title: 'Still' or 'also' with 还
notes.explanation: Put 还 (hái) before a verb or adjective to mean 'still' (continuing) or 'also / in addition' within the same subject.

examples.pinyin: Tā hái zài jiàoshì lǐ kàn shū.
examples.english: He is still reading in the classroom.

examples.chinese: 我买了苹果，还买了西瓜。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ mǎi le píngguǒ, hái mǎi le xīguā.
examples.english: I bought apples, and also bought watermelon.

notes.title: Immediate or early action with 就
notes.explanation: Use 就 (jiù) before a verb to show something happens sooner than expected or right after another event.

examples.pinyin: Tā měitiān liù diǎn jiù qǐchuáng le.
examples.english: He gets up as early as six every day.

examples.pinyin: Xià le kè wǒ jiù huí jiā.
examples.english: I'll go home right after class ends.

notes.title: Starting points with 从…到…
notes.explanation: Pair 从 (cóng, 'from') with 到 (dào, 'to') to express a span in either time or distance.

examples.chinese: 我从星期一到星期五上班。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ cóng xīngqīyī dào xīngqīwǔ shàngbān.
examples.english: I work from Monday to Friday.

examples.chinese: 从这里到地铁站怎么走？
examples.pinyin: Cóng zhèlǐ dào dìtiězhàn zěnme zǒu?
examples.english: How do I get from here to the subway station?

notes.title: Comparing two things with 比
notes.explanation: Put A before 比 (bǐ) and B after it, followed directly by the adjective (without 很). Add 一点儿 or 多了 after to show degree.

examples.english: My older brother is taller than me.
Today is a bit hotter than yesterday.

notes.title: Describing how an action is done with 得
notes.explanation: Insert 得 (de) after a verb to describe how well or in what way the action is performed.

examples.english: He runs very fast.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de Hànyǔ shuō de zhēn hǎo!
examples.english: You speak Chinese really well!

notes.title: Negative commands with 别
notes.explanation: Start a sentence with 别 (bié) before a verb to tell someone 'Don't ...' or ask them to stop doing something.

examples.english: Don't talk, listen carefully!

examples.pinyin: Tiān wǎn le, bié kàn le.
examples.english: It's late, stop watching now.

notes.title: Suggestions and guesses with 吧
notes.explanation: Add 吧 (ba) at the end of a sentence to make a friendly suggestion ('let's ...') or soften a guess ('I suppose').

examples.english: Let's go together.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ lèi le ba, xiūxi yíxià.
examples.english: You must be tired; take a rest.

notes.title: Cause and effect with 因为…所以…
notes.pattern: 因为 + Reason, 所以 + Result
notes.explanation: Mandarin often keeps both 因为 ('because') and 所以 ('so') in the same sentence, whereas English uses only one.

examples.chinese: 因为下雨，所以我没去跑步。
examples.pinyin: Yīnwèi xià yǔ, suǒyǐ wǒ méi qù pǎobù.
examples.english: Because it rained, I didn't go running.

examples.chinese: 因为生病了，所以他今天在家。
examples.pinyin: Yīnwèi shēngbìng le, suǒyǐ tā jīntiān zài jiā.
examples.english: Since he got sick, he is at home today.

notes.title: Concession with 虽然…但是…
notes.pattern: 虽然 + Clause A, 但是 + Clause B
notes.explanation: Pair 虽然 (suīrán, 'although') with 但是 (dànshì, 'but') to link two contrasting facts in one sentence.

examples.chinese: 虽然今天很冷，但是天气很好。
examples.pinyin: Suīrán jīntiān hěn lěng, dànshì tiānqì hěn hǎo.
examples.english: Although today is cold, the weather is great.

examples.chinese: 汉字虽然难，但是很有意思。
examples.pinyin: Hànzì suīrán nán, dànshì hěn yǒu yìsi.
examples.english: Although Chinese characters are hard, they are very interesting.

notes.title: Moving objects before the verb with 把
notes.explanation: Use 把 (bǎ) to put a specific object before the verb when you emphasize how the action changes or moves it.

examples.english: Please close the door.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ zuòyè xiě wán le.
examples.english: I finished writing my homework.

notes.title: Passive sentences with 被
notes.explanation: Put the person or thing affected by an action first, followed by 被 (bèi) and the doer (which can be omitted).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de zìxíngchē bèi tōu le.
examples.english: My bicycle was stolen.

examples.pinyin: Bēizi bèi dìdi dǎ suì le.
examples.english: The cup was broken by my younger brother.

notes.title: Conditionals with 如果…就…
notes.explanation: Introduce a hypothetical situation with 如果 (rúguǒ, 'if') and link the outcome with 就 ('then').

examples.chinese: 如果明天不下雨，我们就去爬山。
examples.pinyin: Rúguǒ míngtiān bú xià yǔ, wǒmen jiù qù páshān.
examples.english: If it doesn't rain tomorrow, we will go hiking.

examples.chinese: 如果你有时间，就来我家玩吧。
examples.pinyin: Rúguǒ nǐ yǒu shíjiān, jiù lái wǒ jiā wán ba.
examples.english: If you have time, come hang out at my place.

notes.title: 'Even more' with 更
notes.explanation: Place 更 (gèng) before an adjective or mental verb to mean 'even more ...' compared to something already good or bad.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā fànguǎn de cài gèng hǎochī.
examples.english: The dishes at this restaurant are even more delicious.

examples.chinese: 今天风很大，比昨天更冷。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān fēng hěn dà, bǐ zuótiān gèng lěng.
examples.english: It's very windy today, even colder than yesterday.

notes.title: Late or 'only then' with 才
notes.explanation: Unlike 就 (early/fast), 才 (cái) shows that an action happened later than expected or only after a condition was met.

examples.pinyin: Tā zuówǎn shíyī diǎn cái huí jiā.
examples.english: He didn't get home until eleven last night.

examples.chinese: 我等了半个小时他才来。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ děng le bàn ge xiǎoshí tā cái lái.
examples.english: He didn't arrive until I had waited half an hour.

notes.title: Turning adjectives into adverbs with 地
notes.explanation: Place 地 (de) after an adjective or manner phrase right before the verb to show the attitude or way an action happens.

examples.chinese: 同学们都在认真地听讲。
examples.pinyin: Tóngxuémen dōu zài rènzhēn de tīngjiǎng.
examples.english: The classmates are all listening attentively.

examples.pinyin: Tā gāoxìng de xiào le qǐlái.
examples.english: He happily started laughing.

notes.title: 'Or' in questions vs. 'had better' with 还是
notes.pattern: Option A + 还是 + Option B?  /  还是 + Verb + 吧
notes.explanation: Use 还是 (háishi) for choices inside questions, or before a verb + 吧 to suggest what someone had better do.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎng hē chá háishi hē kāfēi?
examples.english: Would you like tea or coffee?

examples.chinese: 外面太热了，我们还是坐出租车吧。
examples.pinyin: Wàimiàn tài rè le, wǒmen háishi zuò chūzūchē ba.
examples.english: It's too hot outside; we'd better take a taxi.

notes.title: Expressing purpose with 为了
notes.explanation: Start a sentence with 为了 (wèile, 'in order to / for the sake of') to highlight the goal before stating the action taken.

examples.chinese: 为了学好汉语，她每天练习。
examples.pinyin: Wèile xuéhǎo Hànyǔ, tā měitiān liànxí.
examples.english: To learn Chinese well, she practices every day.

examples.chinese: 为了健康，我少喝甜饮料。
examples.pinyin: Wèile jiànkāng, wǒ shǎo hē tián yǐnliào.
examples.english: For my health, I drink fewer sweet beverages.

notes.title: Equality with 跟…一样
notes.pattern: A + 跟 + B + 一样 (+ Adjective)
notes.explanation: Use 跟 (gēn) ... 一样 (yíyàng) to say A and B are the same, optionally adding an adjective at the end.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de xiǎngfǎ gēn nǐ yíyàng.
examples.english: My idea is the same as yours.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shuāng xié gēn nà shuāng yíyàng guì.
examples.english: This pair of shoes is just as expensive as that one.

notes.title: Sequencing steps with 先…然后…
notes.explanation: Place 先 (xiān, 'first') before the first verb, then introduce the next step with 然后 (ránhòu, 'then').

examples.chinese: 我们先吃饭，然后再去散步。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xiān chī fàn, ránhòu zài qù sànbù.
examples.english: Let's eat first, and then go for a walk.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng xiān xǐ shǒu, ránhòu zuò xià.
examples.english: Please wash your hands first, then sit down.

notes.title: 'Only if' with 只有…才…
notes.pattern: 只有 + Necessary Condition, 才 + Result
notes.explanation: Combine 只有 (zhǐyǒu, 'only') with 才 (cái) to stress that a condition is the sole way to achieve the result.

examples.chinese: 只有多练习，汉语才会进步。
examples.pinyin: Zhǐyǒu duō liànxí, Hànyǔ cái huì jìnbù.
examples.english: Only by practicing more will your Chinese improve.

examples.chinese: 只有努力工作，才能成功。
examples.pinyin: Zhǐyǒu nǔlì gōngzuò, cái néng chénggōng.
examples.english: Only if you work hard can you succeed.

notes.title: 'The more..., the more...' with 越…越…
notes.pattern: Subject + 越 + Verb / Adj 1 + 越 + Adj / Verb 2
notes.explanation: Pair two 越 (yuè) clauses to show that as one quality or action increases, the second changes along with it.

examples.english: The rain is getting heavier and heavier.

examples.pinyin: Hànzì yuè xué yuè yǒu yìsi.
examples.english: The more you study Chinese characters, the more interesting they get.

notes.title: 'Besides' or 'except' with 除了…以外
notes.pattern: 除了 + A (+ 以外), Subject + 还 / 都 + B
notes.explanation: Use 除了 (chúle)... 以外 with 还/也 in the second clause for 'besides/in addition', or with 都 for 'except'.

examples.chinese: 除了英语以外，他还会说日语。
examples.pinyin: Chúle Yīngyǔ yǐwài, tā hái huì shuō Rìyǔ.
examples.english: Besides English, he can also speak Japanese.

examples.chinese: 除了星期天，我每天都上班。
examples.pinyin: Chúle Xīngqītiān, wǒ měitiān dōu shàngbān.
examples.english: Except for Sunday, I work every day.

notes.title: Doing two things at once with 一边…一边…
notes.pattern: Subject + 一边 + Verb 1, 一边 + Verb 2
notes.explanation: Put 一边 (yìbiān) before two verbs performed by the same person at the same time.

examples.chinese: 他喜欢一边听音乐，一边看书。
examples.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan yìbiān tīng yīnyuè, yìbiān kàn shū.
examples.english: He likes listening to music while reading.

examples.chinese: 我们一边走，一边聊天吧。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yìbiān zǒu, yìbiān liáotiān ba.
examples.english: Let's chat while we walk.

notes.title: 'Not only..., but also...' with 不但…而且…
notes.pattern: 不但 + Clause A, 而且 + Clause B
notes.explanation: Use 不但 (búdàn, 'not only') followed by 而且 (érqiě, 'moreover / but also') to build on a first point.

examples.chinese: 这里的水果不但便宜，而且新鲜。
examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ de shuǐguǒ búdàn piányi, érqiě xīnxiān.
examples.english: The fruit here is not only cheap, but also fresh.

examples.chinese: 她不但聪明，而且非常努力。
examples.pinyin: Tā búdàn cōngming, érqiě fēicháng nǔlì.
examples.english: She is not only smart, but also very hardworking.

notes.title: 'Interested in' with 对…感兴趣
notes.pattern: Subject + 对 + Topic + 感兴趣
notes.explanation: Put the topic after 对 (duì) before 感兴趣 (gǎn xìngqù); never place the topic directly after 感兴趣.

examples.chinese: 我对中国历史很感兴趣。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ duì Zhōngguó lìshǐ hěn gǎn xìngqù.
examples.english: I am very interested in Chinese history.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ duì yīnyuè gǎn xìngqù ma?
examples.english: Are you interested in music?
